  \caption{Current delivered into the \SI{10}{\pico\farad} load during the same step, positive out of the amplifier. The asymmetry is plain: while the output slews up the cascoded PMOS mirror holds a flat \SI{14.1}{\micro\ampere}, and while it slews down the output pulls only \SI{3.5}{\micro\ampere}. The narrow spikes at each edge --- \SI{24.4}{\micro\ampere} and \SI{12.6}{\micro\ampere} --- last well under a microsecond; it is the flat sections that set the slew rate. These are slewing currents with the input pair overdriven past its common-mode range, so read them as the shape of the asymmetry rather than as a drive rating; see the discussion following Table~\ref{tab:ctrlamp-largesignal}.}
